subject: PO 74521 — weekly sweep, GL mapping & volume-pricing proration

Subject: PO 74521 — billing expectations and invoice cadence

Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is ready to proceed pending a few procurement items so we can route PO 74521 through AP. High level asks from our side: 

- PO must include a single line item with the charged SKU and a separate PO-level field: billingEntity (our GL mapping) so our ERP can auto-match.
- Invoice cadence: we need weekly invoices (every Monday) but a consolidated monthly statement for reconciliation.
- Net terms: we require net45 for this vendor category.
- Discounts: we have agreed a volume band discount (Tier A 0-50k 3%, Tier B 50k-150k 7%). We need clarity on proration when usage flips bands mid-week/month (linear or cliff?).

I attached the PO template and our billing requirements sheet. Can Redwood confirm that you can put the PO number in the invoice reference and include the billingEntity custom field, and confirm how discounts will be calculated in practice?

Olivia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | MedTide Inc
procurement@medtide.com
(415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: PO 74521 — billing expectations and invoice cadence

Olivia — thanks for the clear note and the template. Looping in Kim (billing ops) and Karthik (finance) to confirm the mechanics. Quick answers up front: 

- We can include PO number in invoice reference and add a billingEntity custom field on every invoice line.
- Weekly invoice cadence is doable; we typically issue a weekly invoice file and can also produce a consolidated monthly statement for your AP team.
- Discount proration: we default to linear proration across billing days (so if usage crosses tiers mid-week, discount is prorated by usage-volume and days), but we can support cliff behavior if that's a strict requirement — would need it in the SOW/PO.

Kim — can you confirm the export format (CSV vs XML) for your ERP consumers and whether including billingEntity breaks any of our current batching?

Next steps: if you confirm linear proration is acceptable, I can send a one-page addendum describing the invoice fields and sample weekly invoice layout for your ERP to validate. If you require cliff behavior, we’ll need to model revenue recognition and show expected price impact.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: PO field mapping & discount behavior recommendation

Fyi — I reviewed the MedTide template. A few operational notes: 

1) Export format: we can deliver weekly invoices as CSV export; our billing system can also emit an XML/EDIFACT feed if their ERP needs that.
2) billingEntity: we can add a free-text field, but to support automatic match we prefer a short code (e.g., MT-GL-4123). I recommend we supply both: billingEntity (free text) + billingCode (canonical code).
3) Discounts: cliff proration is operationally simpler (apply the higher/lower discount to the entire invoice period once usage crosses the band) but is more likely to create step-changes that AP dislikes. Linear proration spreads the delta across days and aligns with usage-driven billing.

Recommendation: propose linear proration by default, include an explicit clause in the PO that MedTide can request cliff processing at quarter boundaries only (requires 30-day notice). That minimizes exceptions.

I can draft the one-page invoice schema that Mateo referenced and include sample CSV columns: invoice_date, invoice_period_start, invoice_period_end, invoice_number, po_number, billingEntity, billingCode, sku, units, unit_price, discount_pct, net_amount, reference_url.

Kimberly Park
Billing Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

Olivia / Mateo — a couple of finance-side constraints to flag: 

- Net45 request: acceptable for enterprise customers but will impact our cash conversion. We can agree to net45 on a contracted basis for DEAL-9812, but we will need a bill run posting schedule in the contract (i.e., weekly invoices issued on Monday, payments due 45 days from invoice_date).
- Weekly sweep: operationally OK, but note that weekly invoices increase AP ticket volume. If MedTide would accept bi-weekly plus a weekly interim CSV for early reconciliation, that reduces AP strain for us and your team — it's a tradeoff.
- GL mapping: we require that MedTide provide a stable billingCode mapping (billingCode values) ahead of first invoice; mismatches will delay payment and could create disputes.

If they need strict weekly invoices, we can support but will ask for a clause limiting disputed-amount adjustments to 60 days from invoice date to avoid long tail reconciliation.

—Karthik Iyer
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
